title: Paddle
content:
## Overview

Paddle is a merchant of record payment platform that handles subscription billing, sales tax compliance, and global payments infrastructure. Integrating Paddle with your Emergent app enables you to accept payments, manage subscriptions, and handle customer billing without building your own payment infrastructure.

This guide walks you through connecting Paddle to your Emergent application using environment variables and the Paddle SDK.

<Note>
Paddle acts as the merchant of record, meaning they handle all payment processing, tax calculation, and compliance requirements on your behalf.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need:

- A Paddle account (sign up at [paddle.com](https://paddle.com))
- Access to your Paddle dashboard
- Your Paddle API credentials (Vendor ID and API Key)
- An Emergent app where you want to accept payments

## Getting Your Paddle Credentials

<Steps>
<Step title="Log in to your Paddle dashboard">
Navigate to [vendors.paddle.com](https://vendors.paddle.com) and sign in to your account.
</Step>

<Step title="Locate your Vendor ID">
Your Vendor ID is displayed in the top-right corner of the dashboard. It's a numeric identifier unique to your account.
</Step>

<Step title="Generate an API Key">
Go to **Developer Tools → Authentication** in the sidebar, then click **Generate Key**. Store this key securely — it won't be shown again.

<Warning>
Treat your API Key like a password. Never commit it to version control or expose it in client-side code.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Configure webhook secrets (optional)">
If you plan to receive webhook events from Paddle (for subscription updates, payment confirmations, etc.), generate a webhook secret under **Developer Tools → Notifications**. Save this for later configuration.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Adding Paddle to Your Emergent App

<Steps>
<Step title="Set environment variables">
In your Emergent app's chat interface, tell the AI to add the following environment variables:

```
PADDLE_VENDOR_ID=your_vendor_id
PADDLE_API_KEY=your_api_key
PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_webhook_secret
```

Replace the placeholder values with your actual Paddle credentials. The AI will securely store these in your app's environment.
</Step>

<Step title="Install the Paddle SDK">
Ask the AI to install the appropriate Paddle SDK for your app's stack:

<CodeGroup>
```bash Node.js
npm install @paddle/paddle-node-sdk
```

```bash Python
pip install paddle-billing
```

```bash PHP
composer require paddle/paddle-php-sdk
```
</CodeGroup>
</Step>

<Step title="Initialize the Paddle client">
Describe to the AI how you want to use Paddle. For example:

> "Create a Paddle client using the environment variables. I want to be able to create checkout sessions and handle webhook events for subscription updates."

The AI will generate the necessary initialization code and integration logic.
</Step>

<Step title="Test the integration">
Ask the AI to create a test checkout flow. Paddle provides a sandbox environment for testing without processing real payments. Tell the AI:

> "Create a test payment page that uses Paddle's sandbox mode. Add a button to initiate a checkout for a $10 monthly subscription."
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common Use Cases

<Tabs>
<Tab title="One-time Payments">
For single purchases, create a checkout session with a one-time product:

- Define your product in the Paddle dashboard
- Create a checkout link or overlay using the Product ID
- Handle the `payment.succeeded` webhook to fulfill the order
</Tab>

<Tab title="Subscriptions">
For recurring billing:

- Set up a subscription plan in Paddle with your desired billing interval
- Create checkout sessions that reference the plan
- Listen for `subscription.created`, `subscription.updated`, and `subscription.canceled` webhooks
- Update user access based on subscription status
</Tab>

<Tab title="Usage-based Billing">
For metered usage:

- Create a usage-based pricing plan in Paddle
- Report usage events via the API as customers consume resources
- Paddle automatically calculates charges based on reported usage
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Handling Webhooks

Paddle sends webhook events to notify your app of payment and subscription changes. Configure a webhook endpoint in your app to receive these events.

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a webhook route">
Ask the AI to create an endpoint that receives POST requests from Paddle:

> "Create a `/webhooks/paddle` endpoint that verifies the webhook signature using `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and processes incoming events."
</Step>

<Step title="Add the webhook URL in Paddle">
In your Paddle dashboard, go to **Developer Tools → Notifications** and add your webhook URL:

```
https://your-app.emergent.build/webhooks/paddle
```

<Info>
If you're using a [custom domain](/custom-domain), use that domain in your webhook URL instead.
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Handle key events">
Tell the AI which events matter for your business logic. Common events include:

- `payment.succeeded` — Payment completed successfully
- `subscription.created` — New subscription started
- `subscription.updated` — Subscription changed (plan upgrade/downgrade)
- `subscription.canceled` — Subscription ended
- `transaction.completed` — Transaction finalized
</Step>
</Steps>

## Testing Your Integration

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="How do I test without real payments?">
Paddle provides a sandbox environment for testing. In your Paddle dashboard, toggle to **Sandbox** mode in the top navigation. Use sandbox credentials in your `PADDLE_VENDOR_ID` and `PADDLE_API_KEY` environment variables during development.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I simulate different payment scenarios?">
In sandbox mode, Paddle provides test card numbers that simulate various outcomes (successful payments, declined cards, 3D Secure challenges, etc.). Check Paddle's documentation for the full list of test credentials.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I verify webhooks are working?">
Use the **Event Log** in your Paddle dashboard to see all webhook deliveries. You can also manually resend events to test your endpoint's handling logic.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Going Live

When you're ready to accept real payments:

<Steps>
<Step title="Complete Paddle's verification process">
Submit your business details and complete any required verification steps in the Paddle dashboard.
</Step>

<Step title="Switch to production credentials">
Update your environment variables with your production Vendor ID and API Key (not the sandbox credentials).
</Step>

<Step title="Update webhook URLs">
Ensure your webhook endpoint is configured with your production domain and is publicly accessible.
</Step>

<Step title="Test a real transaction">
Process a small test payment using a real card to confirm everything works end-to-end.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Troubleshooting

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Checkout not loading" icon="circle-exclamation">
Verify your `PADDLE_VENDOR_ID` is correct and matches the environment (sandbox vs. production) you're using.
</Card>

<Card title="Webhooks not received" icon="webhook">
Check that your webhook URL is publicly accessible and that the signature verification is using the correct `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
</Card>

<Card title="API authentication errors" icon="key">
Confirm your `PADDLE_API_KEY` is valid and hasn't been regenerated. API keys are environment-specific (sandbox keys don't work in production).
</Card>

<Card title="Tax calculation issues" icon="receipt">
Ensure customer location data is being passed correctly to Paddle. Paddle requires accurate location info for sales tax compliance.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Next Steps

- Explore Paddle's customer portal for self-service subscription management
- Set up email receipts and invoices in your Paddle dashboard
- Implement plan upgrades and downgrades
- Add promo codes and discounts for marketing campaigns

<Tip>
You can describe any payment flow to the Emergent AI in plain English, and it will generate the necessary Paddle integration code. For example: "Add a pricing page with three subscription tiers and handle upgrades between them."
</Tip>
